AST: Aspartate aminotransferase (U/L), an enzyme marker for liver and muscle damage, elevated in hepatic disease, myocardial infarction, or skeletal muscle injury.
Alkalinephos: Alkaline phosphatase (U/L), an enzyme marker for liver, bone, or intestinal function, elevated in hepatobiliary disease or bone disorders.
BUN: Blood urea nitrogen (mg/dL), a marker of kidney function and protein metabolism, elevated in renal failure, dehydration, or high protein intake.
BaseExcess: Base excess (mEq/L), an indicator of metabolic acid-base imbalance, negative in metabolic acidosis and positive in metabolic alkalosis.
Bilirubin_direct: Direct bilirubin (mg/dL), a marker of liver function and biliary obstruction, elevated in cholestasis or hepatocellular disease.
Bilirubin_total: Total bilirubin (mg/dL), a marker of liver function and hemolysis, elevated in hepatobiliary disease, hemolytic anemia, or Gilbert syndrome.
Calcium: Serum calcium (mg/dL), an electrolyte essential for bone health, muscle contraction, nerve function, and blood clotting, abnormal in parathyroid disorders.
Chloride: Serum chloride (mEq/L), an electrolyte important for fluid balance and acid-base status, abnormal in dehydration or metabolic alkalosis.
Creatinine: Serum creatinine (mg/dL), a critical marker of kidney function reflecting glomerular filtration rate, elevated in acute or chronic renal failure.
DBP: Diastolic blood pressure (mmHg), arterial pressure during cardiac relaxation phase, indicator of peripheral vascular resistance.
EtCO2: End-tidal carbon dioxide (mmHg), the partial pressure of CO2 at the end of expiration, a non-invasive marker of ventilation adequacy and cardiac output.
FiO2: Fraction of inspired oxygen (%), the percentage of oxygen in inhaled air delivered to the patient, critical parameter for ventilation management.
Fibrinogen: Fibrinogen (mg/dL), a coagulation factor protein synthesized by the liver, elevated in inflammation or decreased in DIC and liver failure.
Glucose: Blood glucose (mg/dL), a marker of carbohydrate metabolism and diabetes status, critical for detecting hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia in ICU patients.
HCO3: Serum bicarbonate (mEq/L), a key component of acid-base balance, decreased in metabolic acidosis or increased in metabolic alkalosis.
HR: Heart rate (beats per minute), a vital sign reflecting cardiac activity and autonomic function, abnormal in arrhythmias, shock, or fever.
Hct: Hematocrit (%), the percentage of red blood cells in total blood volume, decreased in anemia or increased in polycythemia or dehydration.
Hgb: Hemoglobin (g/dL), the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells, decreased in anemia or blood loss, critical for oxygen delivery assessment.
Lactate: Blood lactate (mmol/L), a marker of tissue hypoxia and anaerobic metabolism, elevated in sepsis, shock, or tissue hypoperfusion.
MAP: Mean arterial pressure (mmHg), the average arterial pressure over a cardiac cycle, critical for assessing organ perfusion (normal 70-100 mmHg).
Magnesium: Serum magnesium (mg/dL), an electrolyte vital for neuromuscular function, cardiac rhythm, and enzyme activity, deficiency can cause arrhythmias and seizures.
O2Sat: Oxygen saturation (%), the percentage of hemoglobin bound to oxygen, measured by pulse oximetry, critical for assessing oxygenation status.
PTT: Partial thromboplastin time (seconds), a coagulation marker measuring intrinsic pathway function, prolonged in heparin therapy or coagulation factor deficiency.
PaCO2: Partial pressure of carbon dioxide in arterial blood (mmHg), reflects respiratory acid-base balance and ventilation adequacy (normal 35-45 mmHg).
Phosphate: Serum phosphate (mg/dL), an electrolyte important for bone health, energy metabolism, and cell function, abnormal in renal failure or malnutrition.
Platelets: Platelet count (cells/mm³), a marker of blood clotting ability, decreased in thrombocytopenia or increased in reactive thrombocytosis.
Potassium: Serum potassium (mEq/L), a critical electrolyte for cardiac rhythm, muscle contraction, and nerve function, abnormal levels can cause fatal arrhythmias.
Resp: Respiratory rate (breaths per minute), a vital sign reflecting pulmonary function and respiratory drive, abnormal in respiratory distress or failure.
SBP: Systolic blood pressure (mmHg), arterial pressure during cardiac contraction phase, indicator of cardiac output and vascular tone.
SaO2: Arterial oxygen saturation (%), the percentage of hemoglobin bound to oxygen in arterial blood, critical for assessing oxygenation status.
Temp: Body temperature (°C or °F), a vital sign reflecting thermoregulation, elevated in infection, inflammation, or hyperthermia.
TroponinI: Troponin I (ng/mL), a highly specific cardiac biomarker for myocardial injury, critical for diagnosing acute myocardial infarction and assessing heart damage.
WBC: White blood cell count (cells/mm³), a marker of immune response and infection, elevated in bacterial infection or leukemia, decreased in immunosuppression.
pH: Blood pH value (7.35-7.45 normal range), an indicator of acid-base balance status, abnormal in respiratory or metabolic acidosis/alkalosis.
